w04.001: The Second Antithesis: The Challenge of Outer Space
w04.002: The Absonite Story, Chapter VII, The Second Antithesis (pp. 75–83)
w04.003: Once the Supreme Being has finished growing, the master universe passes into what may be called the post-Supreme ages. Over four ages, from the third through the sixth, the first experiential Trinity organizes the four levels of outer space, and at the close of that long work God the Ultimate appears. Sadler holds that the outer space creations will lack only one thing: finite experience. That lack becomes an opening for the beings who grew up in the grand universe, and their going out to meet it is what he names the Ultimate Adventure. In this chapter Sadler puts numbers to the administration of the Primary Space Level, looks ahead to a new partnership of dual Deity in which the Spirit joins the Supreme, and considers whether Ultimacy might emerge in several stages rather than at once.
w04.005: Sadler proposes a fresh way of naming the ages, taking the Supreme Being as the point of reference. The present second universe age is the era in which the Supreme is evolving and growing. On that reckoning the first age, which came before, is a pre-Supreme age, and the ages of outer space that follow the completion of the Supreme’s growth can be called post-Supreme ages.
w04.006: The post-Supreme ages number four, namely ages three through six. Each corresponds to one level of outer space. What binds them together, in Sadler’s summary, is that throughout all four the first experiential Trinity labors toward three goals:
w04.007: the unification of the first experiential Trinity itself
w04.008: the completion of the master universe
w04.009: the emergence of God the Ultimate
w04.010: The Urantia Book likewise says that the appearance of the Supreme will open the way to the full functioning of this Trinity.
w04.012: These are the ages when the creative forces and agencies of Paradise reach out on a grand scale into outer space. Beside them go administrators from Paradise and Havona, together with every experiential “veteran” who passed through the evolutionary age of the superuniverses. Sadler finds great meaning in this partnership. For the first time the perfect and the perfected form a single team and take up a common task. He calls this joint undertaking the Ultimate Adventure, a name meant to pair with the Supreme Adventure met in earlier chapters.
w04.013: 2. Cytoplasmic Need Widens Nuclear Function (orig. pp. 76–77)
w04.014: Two experiential Deities refine the potentials
w04.015: Out of what do creators create? Sadler returns to an idea from the previous chapter. The raw material of creation is potential, possibility not yet realized, flowing from the three Absolutes. But because these potentials are absolute, they are of no direct use to creators working on finite levels. Something must first prepare them.
w04.016: In Sadler’s account the preparation happens in two steps. The Ultimate, who stands in immediate touch with the absolute level, first organizes absolute potential so that it becomes responsive to creative action; the Supreme then refines it further, fitting it to finite levels. Both, he says, are already doing this long before their full emergence. One might compare it to ore taken from a mine: a smelter turns it into metal, and a workshop then rolls that metal into usable sheets. Creators are able to “create” only because material has been made ready in this way. The two-step refining is Sadler’s interpretive model. The Urantia Book says that absonite phenomena are acts of the Ultimacy of Deity, but it does not divide the process into stages like a production line.
w04.019: At the passage from the second to the third age, an important change overtakes the potential available for creation and growth. Because the Supreme is growing now, beings created or evolving in this age can share in that growth. When the age closes, however, the Supreme’s growth also closes, and the potential for finite experience is used up. Being finite, it can be exhausted.
w04.020: Sadler illustrates this by comparing two Creative Spirits. A Creative Spirit serving in a local universe today can bring forth seraphim able to grow through finite experience, because she draws on the potential of the growing Supreme. A Creative Spirit who will serve on the Primary Space Level in the third age will be identical in nature to her elder sister, yet she will never produce such seraphim, for the material will no longer exist. She will work with post-Supreme potential, probably subabsolute rather than finite, and her children will be beings who lack any innate capacity for finite experience.
w04.022: What will the universes of outer space be like, and who will their natives be? Sadler admits that he cannot answer in any positive way, since such matters lie wholly beyond the range of our experience. Just as the natives of Havona could not imagine us until they met the first ascending pilgrims, so we cannot picture the beings of outer space. Yet one thing is sure. Nowhere in outer space, and in none of its natives, will there be finite experience. This is not Sadler’s guess; The Urantia Book itself foresees it.
w04.025: It is precisely in this lack that Sadler locates our place. The very quality missing in outer space is one we have received in abundance. We are children of the Supreme. Finite experience lies at the heart of the nature of every experiential and evolutionary being born in the grand universe. As the Supreme has grown in us, we have grown in Him, and so we resemble the Supreme, the God of finite experience.
w04.026: Even as finaliters we will still be unfinished. The Urantia Book describes the finaliters as sixth-stage spirits who have attained destiny only as far as the present age allows.
w04.028: Sadler expects these remaining goals to come within reach through service in outer space. In carrying finite experience into places that have none, and filling that gap, we ourselves will pass beyond our present limits. This retraces the path of our predecessors from Paradise and Havona, who likewise outgrew their own limits by going out to serve in superuniverses that lacked divine perfection.
w04.029: Sadler and the text: the finaliters’ three unreached goals
w04.030: Sadler lists the goals not yet reached by the finaliters as ultimate creature status, finality of creature service, and finality of experiential Deity attainment. The text words the first item as “⟦Q 31:3.6⟧finality of ultimate spirit status⟦/Q⟧” [31:3.6]. The meaning is close, but Sadler has paraphrased. The text also says that not even the finaliters have yet found the Supreme Being, nor are they likely to until they become seventh-stage spirits and the Supreme is actually functioning in the outer universes [56:6.4]. The incompleteness of the finaliters is a statement of the text before it is an interpretation of Sadler’s.
w04.031: 3. The Challenge of the Ultimate Adventure (orig. pp. 77–78)
w04.033: At the dawn of time God set before the citizens of the settled, eternal creation the built-in imperfection of the seven superuniverses. The perfect beings of Paradise-Havona answered that challenge by venturing into the uncertainties of the still unorganized superuniverse space level; that was the Supreme Adventure. At the same moment God offered imperfect creatures the invitation, “Be you perfect, even as I am perfect,” and the forces and personalities of perfection carried that challenge all the way to the evolutionary worlds. Sadler adds that God’s infinite perfection became something we could grasp when Jesus humanized it.
w04.034: Now God challenges all creation a second time. Sadler compares the two challenges as acts of subtraction. In the first, God withheld inborn perfection from the new superuniverses, and the resulting task was to make the imperfect perfect through growth and experience in time and space. In the second, God withholds something again: this time, the possibility of growth through finite experience. Every citizen of the grand universe is called to make up for this lack in the outer creations.
w04.035: Two challenges: what God withheld, and who goes out to fill the gap
w04.037: Sadler believes that by then we will truly have become children of the Supreme Being and so will be able to meet this challenge; even our minds will be linked with the mind of the Supreme. His hope is that, as Jesus revealed the Universal Father, we will reveal God the Supreme to the new creatures of the outer universes. The Urantia Book describes the postfinaliter experience this way.
w04.039: Sadler judges us well equipped for the task, since three things will have been fused in us: the divinity bestowed by the Adjuster, the experiential wisdom hard won on the climb to Paradise, and long service in the growing superuniverses. Out there we will face new problems of sheer vastness, unforeseeable situations, and things we cannot explain. Like new creatures standing at the dawn of a new creation, we will become young again, grow again, and once more know the sudden widening of every horizon.
w04.040: A challenge of breadth and of depth
w04.041: Sadler stresses that this challenge has depth as well as breadth. Before us lie not only the immense time, space and mass of the outer universes but also a renewed search for the Universal Father. Having found the Father as Supreme, can we now find Him as Ultimate? The Urantia Book paints the same picture.
w04.043: 4. Administering the Primary Space Level (orig. pp. 79–81)
w04.045: Sadler now narrows his focus to the third age, the first of the post-Supreme ages, and to the organization of the Primary Space Level. He starts from a few facts supplied by The Urantia Book. Seventy thousand vast aggregations of matter are gathering there, each of them already exceeding any superuniverse in size.
w04.047: Further, the text assigns seventy Master Architects to the Primary Space Level [31:9.6]. From here on the arithmetic is Sadler’s. Dividing seventy thousand aggregations among seventy Architects gives each Architect roughly a thousand.
w04.048: Seven Master Spirits and seventy thousand galaxies
w04.049: Sadler finds good grounds for believing that the Seven Master Spirits will take charge of sectors of outer space continuous with their present superuniverse jurisdictions. If so, each Master Spirit oversees one seventh of the seventy thousand galaxies, ten thousand of them, along with ten Architects. Each of those galaxies is a kind of “super-superuniverse,” larger than any superuniverse.
w04.050: If each Master Spirit shapes the environmental tendencies of an outer space sector as He now shapes those of His own superuniverse, then the Primary Space Level would repeat the pattern of the seven superuniverses on a far grander scale. Seven environments, Father-like, Son-like, Spirit-like, Father-Son-like, Father-Spirit-like, Son-Spirit-like and Father-Son-Spirit-like, would leave an indelible stamp on the natives of each sector. Sadler finds this picture comfortable but too simple, because the Son-Spirit Creative Trios complicate matters considerably once they are counted in.
w04.051: Son-Spirit Creative Trios and forty-nine environments
w04.052: As we saw in Chapter 7, Sadler reasoned that the seven hundred thousand pairs of Creator Sons and Creative Spirits in the local universes would, at the close of the second age, trinitize Associate Creators and so become Son-Spirit Creative Trios. If that reasoning holds, exactly seven hundred thousand Trios will be assigned to outer space.
w04.053: Sadler adds a further point: the Trios will not all be alike. Each Creative Spirit bears the likeness of the Master Spirit of the superuniverse in which she served, so there are seven types of Creative Spirit, and hence seven types of Trio, one hundred thousand of each. Because the currents of the master universe seem to favor variety over uniformity, he expects all seven types to be spread evenly through every Master Spirit’s sector. If one hundred thousand Trios divide the ten thousand galaxies of the first Master Spirit’s sector, each Trio governs about a tenth of a galaxy. That alone is far larger than a tenth of a superuniverse with its hundred thousand local universes.
w04.054: Sadler’s estimated administrative structure for the Primary Space Level. Only the seventy thousand aggregations and the seventy Architects come from The Urantia Book; the rest is Sadler’s division
w04.055: Since each Trio will likewise shape the environment of its own domain, seven environmental tendencies arise within the sector of a single Master Spirit, and across the seven sectors they total 7 × 7 = 49. If the seven superuniverses yield seven types of creature and of Creative Spirit, the Primary Space Level would yield forty-nine distinctive types. Sadler expects this “power of seven” to continue at the next level, giving 343 on the Secondary Space Level. As support he points out that the count of Master Architects for each successive level multiplies by seven in exactly this way [31:9.5–9].
w04.056: Master Architects per space level (text) and number of environmental types (Sadler’s estimate)
w04.061: expected to keep multiplying by seven
w04.062: expected to keep multiplying by seven
w04.063: Universe Sons and Universe Spirits of the third age
w04.064: Finally Sadler turns to the number of Creator Sons. The Urantia Book says that there are already more than seven hundred thousand of them, and that nothing has been revealed about the destiny of those beyond that number.
w04.066: Since there are exactly seven hundred thousand local universes, Sadler infers that the surplus Universe Sons and Universe Spirits will be sent out to organize universes in outer space. The Primary Space Level would then see two or three classes of Universe Sons and Universe Spirits at work. He supposes that the younger Sons and Spirits will serve under the jurisdiction of the Creative Trios, much as the rulers of the major sectors of a superuniverse now relate to the rulers of local universes. Their numbers, he suggests, might reach ten thousand times those who served in the seven superuniverses.
w04.067: 5. The Spirit and the Supreme: Dual Deity of Outer Space (orig. pp. 81–82)
w04.068: A leading partnership for each age
w04.069: Sadler holds that each universe age has its own leading partnership of dual Deity. In the first age the Father-Son led; in the second, the Son-Spirit of the local universes. For the ages after the Supreme emerges, he anticipates a new pairing taking that place: a Spirit-Supreme partnership.
w04.070: The dual-Deity partnership leading each age (Sadler’s scheme)
w04.072: Personalization of the Infinite Spirit; formation of the Paradise Trinity
w04.073: 700,000 Associate Creators; Son-Spirit Creative Trios (Sadler’s conjecture)
w04.075: The Supreme’s function in outer space
w04.076: The Urantia Book speaks of three functions of the Supreme Being. In the central universe He functions as a spirit personality, as a power personality in the grand universe, and His third function, in the master universe, is still latent.
w04.078: The text goes on to report that some believe the Supreme will expand in power as the superalmighty of the outer universes. Sadler declines to choose between “superalmighty” and “mind potential”; he thinks both are likely. Either way, the Supreme will exert a direct and active influence on the outer universes and will work hand in hand with the Spirit.
w04.079: Where the Spirit-Supreme partnership takes shape
w04.080: The Seven Master Spirits are the ones who distribute the Infinite Spirit to the universes beyond Havona. Sadler therefore expects the Spirit-Supreme partnership to be formed chiefly as a bond linking the Supreme with the Master Spirits. This does not mean that the Supreme ceases to cooperate with the Infinite Spirit or breaks off relations with the Creative Spirits. As for what the partnership will produce, Sadler throws up his hands. The Father-Son partnership personalized the Infinite Spirit and led to the Paradise Trinity; the Son-Spirit partnership can give rise to Associate Creators. But for the outcome of the Spirit-Supreme partnership, Sadler himself says, The Urantia Book offers no basis for prediction at all.
w04.081: 6. Stages in the Emergence of the Ultimate (orig. pp. 82–83)
w04.082: Up to this point Sadler has handled the four outer space levels and their four ages together as one block. That is broadly sound, but in one respect the four need to be looked at separately: the emergence of God the Ultimate.
w04.083: The Supreme Being emerges as the outcome of what happens in one age and on one space level. Ultimacy, by contrast, emerges as the outcome of completed creative growth across five ages and five space levels. It follows that the Ultimate’s emergence need not happen all at once; it may unfold in several stages. For instance, the sovereignty of the Ultimate might be established on the Primary Space Level before the Secondary Space Level opens. Ultimate sovereignty would then be a fact on the first level while remaining unrealized on the second, something that never arose while the Supreme was evolving. The same relation could recur between the second and third levels.
w04.084: Supremacy emerges at once; Ultimacy may emerge stage by stage (Sadler’s inference)
w04.085: Sadler thus hints that the first experiential Trinity may be unified in four stages, and that God the Ultimate may likewise emerge in four. The Urantia Book says only that the completed emergence of the Ultimate implies the completion of the master creation [106:4.2]. Emergence in stages is Sadler’s reading of that statement laid out in time sequence.
w04.086: Taking the Supreme Being as reference, Sadler divides the ages into pre-Supreme (first), Supreme (second) and post-Supreme (third to sixth). In the post-Supreme ages the first experiential Trinity works toward three ends: its own unification, a finished master universe, and the appearance of God the Ultimate.
w04.087: In Sadler’s interpretation, absolute potential, the raw material of creation, is refined in steps by the Ultimate and then the Supreme. When the Supreme’s growth ends, the potential for finite experience is exhausted.
w04.088: The Urantia Book says the outer universes will come into being deprived of finite experience, that is, of participation in the Supreme’s evolution. Sadler reads this lack as an opportunity for beings from the grand universe.
w04.089: In the first challenge God withheld perfection; in the second He withholds growth through finite experience. The perfect and the perfected setting out together is the Ultimate Adventure.
w04.090: The seventy thousand aggregations and seventy Architects are figures from the text; ten thousand galaxies per Master Spirit, a tenth of a galaxy per Trio, and forty-nine environments are Sadler’s calculations.
w04.091: Sadler expects the leading dual-Deity partnership to pass from Father-Son through Son-Spirit to Spirit-Supreme, but he makes no forecast of its outcome.
w04.092: Sadler infers that the Ultimate may emerge in stages across the four outer space levels.
w04.094: The Absonite Story, Chapter VIII, Master Universe Magnitudes (pp. 84–87)
w04.095: Having traveled from Havona through the superuniverses into outer space, Sadler pauses to ask how large, how massive and how long-lasting the master universe is. To make spatial size something one can feel, he likens the grand universe to a tennis ball and then enlarges the outer levels step by step into a living room, a city block, a great city and the moon. On mass he gathers the textual clues: seventy thousand aggregations, 375 million galaxies, and the distribution of Paradise gravity. On time he takes the age of the Andronover nebula as a unit and estimates the length of each age.
w04.096: 1. The Size of Space: From a Tennis Ball to the Moon (orig. pp. 84–85)
w04.097: So far in the journey Sadler has paid little attention to size or duration. Now he poses three questions. What is the size of the master universe? What is its mass? What is the duration of each universe age?
w04.098: He begins with the grand universe we know. Havona contains a billion worlds, and the superuniverses are planned to hold seven trillion inhabited worlds. Havona’s dimensions are not known exactly, but our superuniverse, Orvonton, is about half a million light-years across; the text says that Orvonton’s outermost inhabited systems are somewhat under 250,000 light-years from its center [32:2.11]. Leaving Havona aside, the grand universe is therefore roughly a million light-years in diameter.
w04.099: Figures like these soon escape the senses. So instead of numbers Sadler shows proportions with everyday objects. Let the grand universe be a tennis ball. The Primary Space Level is then about the size of a fairly spacious living room. The Secondary Space Level is a long city block raised into a cube, with the living room floating at its center. The Tertiary Space Level is the cube of a great city measuring thirty-two miles (about 51 km) on each side. The Quartan Space Level is a sphere some 3,200 miles (about 5,100 km) across, roughly half again as large as our moon; Sadler proposes to use the moon as the symbol all the same.
w04.100: He invites us to nest these images one inside another in imagination. Float the tennis ball in the middle of the living room, the living room in the middle of the city-block cube, the block in the middle of the city cube, and the city in the middle of the moon. Then return to the tennis ball: it is the whole of today’s organized creation, holding Havona and the seven superuniverses, seven hundred thousand local universes and seven trillion inhabited worlds. Sadler’s closing advice is brief: picture the tennis ball, and then picture the moon.
w04.101: Sadler’s size analogy. With each level crossed, the diameter grows roughly a hundredfold (logarithmic scale)
w04.102: Following the analogy, the diameter grows roughly a hundredfold from one level to the next. Sadler adds that putting the Primary Space Level at a hundred times the grand universe may be far too cautious, and that the true factor could exceed ten thousand. Still, even the cautious estimate is overwhelming enough that he lets it stand. Observations reported in the text offer further clues. A zone of energy activity begins some half a million light-years beyond the periphery of the grand universe and extends for more than twenty-five million light-years; this is the first outer space level [12:1.14]. And more than fifty million light-years beyond its outermost limits, force manifestations of a second level have been detected [12:1.15].
w04.104: There is even less information about mass than about size. Yet it is plain that the physical mass of outer space far exceeds anything known in the grand universe. Sadler sets two passages side by side. One is the seventy thousand aggregations of matter met in the previous chapter. The other concerns new galaxies that astronomers will soon see.
w04.106: Whether the two statements refer to the same physical creation cannot be known. Sadler believes they do, and he places all this mass on the Primary Space Level. A third clue is Paradise gravity. The Urantia Book says that most of the Paradise gravity grasp is already engaged in holding the creations of outer space.
w04.108: These future universes have only just begun and will go on growing for a very long time. Every clue converges: in size and in mass alike, outer space vastly surpasses the grand universe.
w04.109: 3. The Magnitude of Time: the Andronover Time Unit (orig. p. 87)
w04.110: When the lengths of the universe ages are reckoned, the numbers grow too large to handle. Just as interstellar distances are measured in light-years rather than miles, Sadler suggests making one large unit for time as well. He takes as that unit the age of the Andronover nebula, which gave birth to our sun: about a trillion years. He calls it the Andronover Time Unit, or ATU for short. The reason for the choice is that the age of Andronover is the longest span of time given in The Urantia Book.
w04.111: Sadler and the text: the age of Andronover
w04.112: The text says that the Andronover nebula was formally initiated 875 billion years ago. Sadler’s “about a trillion years” is a rounding of this figure.
w04.114: Lengths of the universe ages estimated by Sadler (1 ATU ≈ one trillion years)
w04.121: The numbers in the table simply show how many times longer each age is than the age of Andronover. What deserves notice is that each change of age multiplies the length by a hundred, the same ratio by which the diameter of the space levels grows from one to the next. The calculations behind them appear in Appendices XVI and XVII of the original and are taken up again in our commentary on those appendices.
w04.122: Sadler reckons that the present second age may be about three-quarters spent. Even so, the remaining quarter amounts to more than ten thousand ATU, over ten thousand trillion years. He adds lightly that we have plenty of time to reach Paradise.
w04.123: Sadler puts the diameter of the grand universe at about a million light-years and, likening it to a tennis ball, enlarges the outer levels into a living room, a city block, a great city and the moon.
w04.124: On this analogy the diameter grows roughly a hundredfold with each step outward through the space levels, and Sadler calls even this a conservative estimate.
w04.125: The clues to mass are the seventy thousand aggregations of matter, the 375 million new galaxies, and the text’s statement that about ninety-five per cent of Paradise gravity acts beyond the organized universes.
w04.126: Sadler takes the Andronover nebula’s age (roughly one trillion years; 875 billion in the text) as a unit of time, the ATU.
w04.127: By Sadler’s estimate the universe ages lengthen a hundredfold with each age, from 50,000 ATU for the second age to 5 trillion ATU for the sixth.
w04.128: The time still remaining in the present age alone exceeds ten thousand ATU.
w04.129: The Second Synthesis: God the Ultimate
w04.130: The Absonite Story, Chapter IX, Second Synthesis: God the Ultimate (pp. 88–94)
w04.131: The master universe is vast, but it has an end. When its growth reaches the edge of the last space level, the second round of thesis, antithesis and synthesis comes to completion. The first synthesis, the Supreme, turns into the second thesis, the first experiential Trinity; that Trinity organizes the second antithesis, the cytoplasmic outer universes, and finally binds them into one with the nuclear grand universe. On the Deity level this second synthesis appears as the final emergence of God the Ultimate. Sadler explains Ultimacy by comparison with Supremacy, sees the seven levels of total Deity completed here, and then surveys the finished master universe from the center outward.
w04.132: 1. A Master Universe with Boundaries (orig. p. 88)
w04.133: The master universe is immense, yet it is limited. Even the outermost level of outer space ends somewhere. Given enough time that edge will be reached, and in eternity there is time enough. The Urantia Book, too, regards the master universe as a bounded creation.
w04.135: The same paragraph mentions those who suppose that beyond the fourth space level there may be an ever-expanding universe of infinity. Sadler sets this aside for the last part of his book and concentrates first on the moment when the growth of the master universe comes to an end.
w04.136: 2. The Unification of the First Experiential Trinity (orig. pp. 88–89)
w04.137: Looking back on the first cycle
w04.138: A finished master universe sets the second great synthesis before us. Sadler first retraces the first cycle. The first thesis was the perfect central creation, standing as a challenge. The first antithesis was the built-in incompleteness of the seven superuniverses. The first synthesis came when the seven superuniverses, settled in light and life, gained perfected status and entered into finite harmony with the perfect central creation. On the Deity level this synthesis appeared as the final emergence of the Supreme Being: God the Supreme, a spirit personality, became one with the experiential sovereign power of the Almighty that had risen out of time and space. It was the completion of the power-personality synthesis with respect to the whole of finite reality.
w04.139: The synthesis becomes a thesis again
w04.140: Once the Supreme has appeared, a new Trinity can become actual, and as it does, the first synthesis turns into the second thesis. That second thesis is the first experiential Trinity. Taking the new nuclear universe, the grand universe, as a fresh power base, it reaches out into outer space, accompanied by countless creators and cooperating creatures. The second antithesis is the outer space universes, which play the part of the cytoplasm. These post-Supreme creations differ from anything that has yet appeared anywhere in the master creation.
w04.141: Two cycles of thesis, antithesis and synthesis. The first synthesis, Supremacy, becomes the second thesis, the first experiential Trinity
w04.143: Here Sadler raises an intriguing question. The Paradise Trinity could have created an existential universe as large as the whole master creation. But to what end? It would have been nothing more than Havona on a bigger scale. A gigantic creation endowed with inborn perfection would have added quantity, not quality, to actual existential divinity. Sadler supposes that Havona was designed just large enough to serve as the proper pattern for every universe that came after it. Thanks to what he calls the “quantitative restraint” of the Paradise Trinity, the first experiential Trinity can appear and collaborate, and the master universe is built not as a copy of Havona but as a new and different experiential creation. The Urantia Book calls Havona a finished portrait of the Supreme’s future perfection.
w04.146: The completion of the master universe is the fruit of the first experiential Trinity’s successful effort to become a unified Deity reality, as the Paradise Trinity is. Sadler sums up three stages in the life of the Trinity Ultimate. Even before the Supreme Being emerged, this Trinity was already a qualified reality. When the Supreme fully emerges and its membership is complete, it becomes a factual reality. When the master universe is finished, it achieves the final power-personality synthesis and becomes a fully unified reality. On the first stage the text speaks directly.
w04.148: When the whole master universe has been completed and the Trinity Ultimate unified, the second synthesis becomes possible: the nucleus, the grand universe, and the cytoplasm, the outer universes, become one. On the Deity level this synthesis shows itself as God the Ultimate emerging at last, the experiential sovereign of the master creation.
w04.150: 3. The Emergence of God the Ultimate (orig. pp. 89–91)
w04.152: Throughout the long ages of master universe growth, God the Ultimate slowly emerges from the status of unknowable, incomplete Deity to that of knowable, experientially completed Deity. Mortals become aware of the challenge of Ultimacy from the time they enter the Corps of the Finality. Once the Supreme has been attained, Ultimacy becomes the goal of experiential Deity seeking for finaliters and every other growing being.
w04.153: Sadler brings back the analogy of the previous chapter. Completing the Supreme takes a domain the size of a tennis ball; completing Ultimacy takes one the size of the moon. If the perfecting of the superuniverses takes “one hour of eternity,” then, he estimates, completing the master universe takes “ten thousand years of eternity”: a considerable span even by the standard of eternal Havona.
w04.155: Among the experiential Deities, God the Ultimate comes second. Sadler explains Ultimacy by setting it alongside Supremacy. The Urantia Book introduces God the Ultimate as follows.
w04.165: Sadler stresses that the Ultimate is not merely a “super-Supreme.” Ultimacy is greater not only in quantity but also in qualitative complexity. On this point he agrees exactly with the text.
w04.167: Inside the confines of the master creation, Ultimacy is truly omnipresent, omnipotent and omniscient. This matches the text’s description of the seventh level of total Deity.
w04.170: Sadler supposes that the Ultimate will be found by no creature until He is found by all, extending to Ultimacy what The Urantia Book says of the Supreme.
w04.172: Yet when at last we do find the Ultimate, we will understand Him, and in that understanding we will come to know the Father as Ultimate. For Sadler, this is where the absonite search for the Universal Father reaches its goal.
w04.173: 4. The Seven Levels of Total Deity Completed (orig. pp. 90–92)
w04.174: With the emergence of God the Ultimate, the seventh level of total Deity function is complete. Here Sadler retraces in one sweep the road of the earlier chapters: Deity before creation, moving from stillness to planning and from planning to action; creative Deity, drawing on the Absolutes of potentiality to bring forth the universes after Havona; evolving Deity, growing in time and through experience; and Deity on the supreme level, interacting on finite levels. Now, on the seventh level, the two Trinities, the existential Trinity and the first experiential Trinity, act together in association with God the Ultimate.
w04.175: Sadler regroups the seven levels into three clusters: three levels before creation, two that go outward, and two that gather inward. On the last two, it is the Supreme and the Ultimate who achieve experiential unification, the final power-personality synthesis. The original closes the chapter with a summary of the seven levels; set against the earlier chapters of this book, it can be arranged as follows.
w04.176: The seven levels of total Deity and where they appear (reconstructed from Sadler’s summary)
w04.180: Unity in the Universal Absolute and the Paradise Trinity
w04.181: Brings forth new things and beings from potential; God the Sevenfold
w04.182: Creation joined with time; creatures take part
w04.183: Unifies all finite activity in the Supreme
w04.184: Unifies all absonite activity in the Ultimate
w04.185: 5. A Tour of the Completed Master Universe (orig. pp. 91–94)
w04.187: The completion and unification of the master universe, from Havona out to the last level of outer space, is an awe-inspiring prospect. Sadler surveys it from the center outward, beginning with the central universe. The divine central universe holds much that lies beyond the finite, and he expects some of its meanings and values to be functionally coordinated with the master universe toward the close of the sixth age. Because the final emergence of the Ultimate marks the end of absonite experiential growth, post-ultimate growth must begin. Such growth goes beyond the ultimate, and whatever goes beyond the ultimate is absolute, or at least coabsolute. Sadler believes that post-ultimate phases of Havona life, never yet entered by experiential beings, will then open. At the same time he is certain of one thing: no development, inside the master universe or outside it, will exceed the capacities and functions of the central creation, the pattern universe.
w04.188: The grand universe: a second breakthrough
w04.189: The grand universe will probably remain under the rule of the Supreme while also coming under the overarching sovereignty of the Ultimate. The superuniverses now break through the barrier of experiential growth for the second time. The first breakthrough came when the Supreme emerged: absonite growth was superimposed on the finite limits of settlement in light and life. The second comes with the final emergence of the Ultimate: post-ultimate potential is superimposed on the limits of completed absonite growth, and the inner universes stand before the unfathomable possibilities of coabsolute expansion.
w04.190: What will a planet like Urantia look like then? Sadler answers with a single comparison. A great distance in civilization and culture separates a world long settled in the last stage of light and life from a primitive planet in its cave-dwelling era. A world in the post-ultimate stage will be still farther removed from a world settled in light and life. Nothing can be said except that it is beyond imagining.
w04.191: The outer universes and the master universe as a whole
w04.192: The master universe is now unified under the experiential sovereignty of the Ultimate. From the Father’s circuits near Paradise to the outermost edge of the fourth space level, this is also the domain in which the first experiential Trinity functions. The outer universes break through the limits of experiential growth for the first time, transcending the limits of absonite growth. So the whole master universe stands at the threshold of post-ultimate growth, and Sadler thinks this probably completes the story of creation.
w04.194: The Master Architects are the living blueprint of the entire master universe, the eternal personalization of God’s whole plan for the master creation. Now that the plan has become actual, they have fulfilled their appointed function as universe planners. But Sadler asks whether their work is also finished as regards the inward, deepening growth that the master universe may undergo on post-ultimate levels. Growth on the supreme (finite) and ultimate (absonite) levels has been achieved, yet even after the sixth age, potentials of a supreme-ultimate nature seem to remain unrealized.
w04.195: Here the study of the master universe’s outward, expanding growth comes to a close. The story of its inward, deepening growth, however, has not ended. As we have seen, whenever a great synthesis is completed it begins to turn into a new thesis. Sadler ends the chapter by turning his gaze beyond the sixth age to the master universe of the post-ultimate ages. That is where the Last Story begins.
w04.196: The master universe is vast but bounded, and the end of its growth completes the second round of thesis, antithesis and synthesis.
w04.197: The first synthesis, the emergence of the Supreme, becomes the second thesis, the first experiential Trinity, which uses the nuclear grand universe as its base to organize the second antithesis, the cytoplasmic outer universes.
w04.198: Sadler holds that the “quantitative restraint” of the Paradise Trinity in not making a larger Havona allows the master universe to become a new and different experiential creation.
w04.199: The Trinity Ultimate passes from qualified reality through factual reality to fully unified reality; with its unification God the Ultimate finally emerges.
w04.200: Ultimacy is the Deity of absonite growth, omnipotent, omniscient and omnipresent within the master universe; as the text says, the Ultimate is not merely an amplification of the Supreme.
w04.201: The emergence of the Ultimate completes the seventh level of total Deity. Sadler groups the seven levels into three clusters: before creation, going outward, and gathering inward.
w04.202: Every domain of the completed master universe stands at the threshold of post-ultimate growth, and supreme-ultimate potentials still remain, opening the next story.
w05.002: The Last Story, Chapter X, The Final Creative Thesis (pp. 95–100)
w05.003: The third block of Sadler's narrative, which he names the Last Story, opens where the second one closed: with a finished master universe now governed in experience by God the Ultimate. Sadler brings back his four tests for recognizing a nuclear universe and reasons that the completed master universe may itself be the third and last nucleus of something larger still. The Trinity Absolute, which becomes a fact once God the Ultimate has emerged, is the final creative thesis; under its direction every resource of the master universe is to be marshaled once more, and the Absolute Adventure begins. That, in outline, is the argument of this chapter.
w05.004: 1. A Story That Can Be Begun but Not Finished (orig. p. 95)
w05.005: Sadler has divided the history of the master universe into three stories. The Finite Story ends with the emergence of God the Supreme; the Absonite Story ends with the emergence of God the Ultimate; and now comes the Last Story. Each of the first two had a beginning and an end. The third is different, and Sadler admits at the outset that he can open it but cannot bring it to a close.
w05.006: The point of departure is the master universe settled from Havona out to the Quartan Space Level and governed experientially by God the Ultimate. The architecture repeats that of the Finite Story: a final creative thesis, the beginning of a final antithesis, and an "impossible synthesis," each in its own chapter.
w05.007: Sadler warns in advance that this story will end in suspense and bewilderment. The powers and agencies of experiential creation, having used up every possibility of growth on the finite and absonite levels, find themselves at a loss before the boundless growth of absolute levels. He names this the last challenge of all, the challenge of infinity.
w05.008: How to Read the Last Story
w05.009: The Urantia Book says very little about what lies beyond the master universe. What it does state plainly is the composition of the Trinity Absolute, a hint that its function will reach past the master universe, and a cautious outlook on the experiential appearance of God the Absolute. Everything else is Sadler applying the rules of his first two stories to the third, so here more than anywhere the reader must keep the revealed text and the conjecture carefully apart.
w05.010: 2. The Master Universe as the Third Nuclear Universe (orig. pp. 96–97)
w05.011: Is the master universe an end in itself?
w05.012: The completion of the master universe is an immensely distant goal. But is it the final goal? Sadler raises the question: might this vast creation be, in truth, a nucleus, the center of something greater? Could cytoplasmic universes one day take shape out past the farthest edge of the Quartan Space Level?
w05.013: So far Sadler has examined two nuclear universes (Chapter 8). Havona serves as the core of the grand universe, which in turn serves as the core of the master universe. Now he proposes a third possibility: the whole master universe may be the third and final nucleus.
w05.015: Sadler uses four criteria to identify a nuclear universe. A nucleus differs in nature from the cytoplasmic creation around it. When a nucleus is completed, a new Deity appears. When a nucleus is completed, a new Trinity becomes factual. And a nucleus hands on its own character to the outer creation through that new Trinity and through the creators and administrators who work with it. Laid against Havona, the grand universe, and the master universe in turn, these four measures give the following picture.
w05.016: Four tests of a nuclear universe and the three nuclei (Sadler's scheme)
w05.018: The stage on which the Supreme Being evolved
The stage on which Ultimacy grew and eventuated
w05.021: God the Sevenfold and the ministering orders
The first experiential Trinity with its associate creators
The whole master universe, mobilized by the second experiential Trinity
w05.022: The logic of the first test is simple. Any creation that follows the master universe will bear a post-Ultimate stamp and so cannot resemble it. Under the fourth test Sadler expects the second experiential Trinity to convey the meaning-values experienced on finite and absonite levels out to the future creations beyond.
w05.023: Nucleus within nucleus: Havona, the grand universe, the master universe, and the Cosmos Infinite that Sadler postulates
w05.024: From this comparison Sadler concludes that the master universe is not a finished end product but one more nuclear creation. Like ripples spreading ring by ring from a stone dropped in a pond, every completed nucleus has opened a wider domain around itself, and the master universe, too, looks like the nucleus of a still larger domain outside it. The Urantia Book points in the same direction.
w05.026: 3. The Trinity Absolute: The Final Creative Thesis (orig. pp. 98–100)
w05.028: The completion of the third nuclear universe and the factualization of the second experiential Trinity are, for Sadler, the third and last creative thesis, the last challenge God sets before every creation. What makes this challenge real is a new Trinity that can take form only when God the Ultimate has entered the field of action, namely the Trinity Absolute.
w05.030: This Trinity gathers into itself the sum of all experiential achievement throughout the master universe, and to that sum one unpredictable factor is added: the presence of the Consummator of Universe Destiny. Sadler reassesses the three members one by one.
w05.031: The Supreme Being: a Deity in both Trinities
w05.032: The Supreme Being belongs to both experiential Trinities, yet Sadler holds that the two memberships are on different levels. When the second age draws to its close, the Supreme completes the power-personality synthesis of the whole finite and becomes a Deity whom creatures can contact. It is as the Deity of the entire finite that the Supreme takes part in the first experiential Trinity.
w05.033: By the end of the sixth age, Sadler thinks, the Supreme Being will be far greater than that. Through the ages of outer space He will have shared in the unifying labors of the Ultimate Trinity and in the affairs of the outer universes, growing on the absonite level as well. If so, the Supreme of the first experiential Trinity is post-finite, while the Supreme of the second is post-Ultimate.
w05.034: God the Ultimate: the synthesis of the whole absonite
w05.035: The completed eventuation of Ultimacy means that God the Ultimate has gathered into His own being everything the master universe has come to mean and to value in experience. To these, Sadler adds, are joined the original absonite values first received from the Paradise Trinity. As Supremacy finishes growing with respect to the whole finite, so Ultimacy finishes growing with respect to the whole absonite. The final eventuation of the Ultimate is therefore the sign that the possibilities of further absonite growth have run out.
w05.036: Sadler's Reasoning: The Post-Ultimate Cannot Be Subabsolute
w05.037: Sadler argues that whatever has passed beyond the ultimate level can no longer remain subabsolute; in some sense it must be absolute (the fuller discussion is in Appendix XIX). On this logic both the Supreme and the Ultimate are post-Ultimate Deities within the second experiential Trinity, and it becomes natural to call that Trinity "absolute." Like the claim that the Supreme also grows on the absonite level, this is Sadler's interpretation, not something The Urantia Book itself states.
w05.039: The third member is the most mysterious being recorded in The Urantia Book. Beyond a connection with the consummation of destiny, almost nothing is known.
w05.041: Sadler offers one careful comparison. Just as the Architects of the Master Universe existed before the other two members of the first experiential Trinity, the Consummator may have existed before the Supreme and the Ultimate. What this being might contribute to destiny, however, Sadler declines even to guess, and that restraint is itself a mark of honesty.
w05.044: Sadler finds the reason for the name in two facts: the members are at least post-Ultimate beings, and the range of their function seems to embrace the whole master universe and to stretch into the space beyond it. Where the first experiential Trinity functions ultimately, the second functions absolutely. The text, too, admits that this Trinity resists easy classification.
w05.046: Sadler sets the goals of the two experiential Trinities side by side and finds that they share one pattern. The first sought to unify itself, to perfect the master universe, and to bring about the eventuation of God the Ultimate. The second seeks to unify itself, to perfect the creations lying outside the master universe, and at last to bring forth God the Absolute. Because these later goals appear to have no limit, they will be enormously hard to reach. Even so, the Trinity Absolute is the fruit of a fully completed master universe and the last challenge set before the citizens of the post-Ultimate age.
w05.047: The make-up and threefold goals of the two experiential Trinities; the Supreme Being belongs to both
w05.049: That the resources of the entire master universe should be mobilized all at once lies beyond imagination. Sadler nonetheless believes that under the direction of the Trinity Absolute this will surely happen, and he bases the belief on the two mobilizations that came before.
w05.050: The first took place at the dawn of time. Citizens of the perfect creation of eternity, challenged by the opening of the imperfect superuniverses, went out to the superuniverse space level; this was the Supreme Adventure of the second age. The second came after the third universe age began, when the Ultimate Trinity gathered every resource of the grand universe and moved into outer space; Sadler calls it the Ultimate Adventure. The third mobilization gathers every resource of the master universe, Havona and all four outer levels included, and Sadler expects this great muster to announce the Absolute Adventure.
w05.051: The Urantia Book describes what will set the second mobilization in motion: the perfected citizens of the superuniverses may rest for a while, but not for long.
w05.053: Sadler and the Text: Names for the Adventures
w05.054: "Supreme adventure" is a phrase the text itself uses more than once [1:0.6]. Sadler writes that the text calls the second mobilization the "Ultimate Adventure," but that exact expression cannot be found in The Urantia Book. The text instead describes the spectacle of the "⟦Q 117:7.17⟧alluring absonite quest⟦/Q⟧" [117:7.17]. "Absolute Adventure" is likewise not the text's phrase; Sadler coined it to match the two earlier names.
w05.055: The three mobilizations repeat a single pattern. The citizens of a completed nucleus receive a new challenge from God and set out, with all that they possess, into a wider outer domain.
w05.056: The Last Story starts from the completed master universe, and Sadler himself says it is a story he can begin but cannot end.
w05.057: Applying the four tests of a nuclear universe (distinctive nature, new Deity, new Trinity, outward transmission) makes the master universe look like the third and last nucleus.
w05.058: The Trinity Absolute consists of God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and the Consummator of Universe Destiny; Sadler regards it as God's final creative thesis.
w05.059: Sadler infers that the Supreme also grows on the absonite level and therefore joins the second Trinity as a post-Ultimate Deity.
w05.060: The first Trinity aimed at perfecting the master universe and bringing forth God the Ultimate; the second aims at perfecting what lies beyond it and bringing forth God the Absolute.
w05.061: After the Supreme Adventure and the Ultimate Adventure, Sadler foresees a last mobilization of the whole master universe that will open the Absolute Adventure.
w05.063: The Last Story, Chapter XI, Beginning of the Final Antithesis (pp. 101–109)
w05.064: The post-Ultimate age begins in time but never ends, and within it one period follows another without limit, each achieved goal opening a more distant one. Sadler holds that mortals do not plunge into eternity and infinity all at once but adjust to them slowly. He illustrates the growth of time sense with simple arithmetic and pictures the adjustment to infinity with a football story. Three times, he argues, God has created a new need by taking something away; at the last He presents the Cosmos Infinite, a realm emptied of every possibility of finite and absonite experience, as the final antithesis.
w05.066: As he begins to study the final antithesis, Sadler loses his familiar landmarks for the first time. He has crossed the boundary of the outermost space level and passed the end of the sixth universe age. For events beyond the master universe even the Master Architects can no longer show the way. So he begins by forging vocabulary for times and places immeasurably far from here and now.
w05.067: Just as what follows the appearance of the central creation in eternity is called "post-Havona," Sadler has called what comes after the grand universe is finished and the Supreme has emerged "post-Supreme." The events after the final eventuation of God the Ultimate he now calls "post-Ultimate."
w05.070: The universe ages differ in quantity: from the second to the sixth they grow steadily longer. Some differ in quality as well. The second age is the one age of Supreme growth, and the four ages of outer space are alike in being post-Supreme ages, ages of the experiential growth of Ultimacy. The post-Ultimate age is new and qualitatively unlike everything before it. Sadler counts seven differences:
w05.071: The master universe has finished growing.
w05.072: Supremacy has completed its post-finite (absonite) growth.
w05.073: The first experiential Trinity is fully unified.
w05.074: God the Ultimate has finally eventuated.
w05.075: The second experiential Trinity has become factual.
w05.076: The potential for absonite growth is exhausted.
w05.077: The absonite search for the Father in His ultimate aspect is over.
w05.078: A last age without an end
w05.079: There is one further difference: this age appears to have no ending in time. Sadler proposes to call it the Final Age, and in this respect it mirrors the first age. The first age, without a beginning in time, nevertheless ends in time; the Final Age begins in time but has no end in time. Both are eternal ages.
w05.080: An eternal age, Sadler insists, need not be a featureless "gray smudge" stretching on forever. He finds a clue in planetary history. The story of an inhabited world falls into seven mortal epochs, and the last, the age of light and life, seems to run on without end. A closer look at the text, however, shows that this age too is divided into seven stages.
w05.082: Sadler surmises that the seventh stage, examined closely, would itself break into seven substages, and that the post-Ultimate age will be built the same way. Each period has a beginning, an end, and goals that can actually be reached. Only the very last period of a series fails to close; instead it launches a new series of growth stages and points toward a larger and fresher horizon, much as a climber who gains one summit sees a higher one rising beyond it.
w05.084: The quality and the quantity of eternity
w05.085: The Urantia Book teaches that ascending mortals become "children of eternity" after the final transit slumber between the inner circuit of Havona and Paradise.
w05.087: Sadler regards this as a fine introduction to the quality of eternity but an insufficient basis for grasping its quantity. A sense of the quantity of eternity, he believes, unfolds gradually in the awareness of mortals, of ascenders, and of finaliters, and the process begins here and now.
w05.089: Sadler distinguishes objective time, measured by the clock, from subjective time, felt in consciousness. Clock time always moves at the same pace. Subjective time drags in boredom and races in delight. Beneath these daily fluctuations there is also a long-term drift: the longer one lives, the faster time seems to go. To a ten-year-old a summer vacation is a small slice of forever; to a forty-year-old three months are short.
w05.090: Sadler works this out with arithmetic. Someone past forty can look back on at least three decades with memory and feeling. A person who can feel that much of the past can, he reasons, also feel forward into an equal stretch of the future. The "time-base" against which the present is judged then becomes sixty years: thirty behind and thirty ahead. The capacity to handle time is thus growing twice as fast as time actually passes. The Urantia Book likewise links maturity with the scale of time awareness.
w05.092: What Sadler finds striking is that after Adjuster fusion this ratio should double again. According to the text, the Adjuster brings the fused ascender the experience and memory of past eternity.
w05.094: At fusion an endless past suddenly opens before the new ascender. Sadler supposes that the ascender can assimilate this memory only in proportion to the span he has consciously lived. One who has spent a thousand years on the mansion worlds could take in another thousand years from the Adjuster's memory. He would then feel two thousand years of past and look ahead across two thousand years of future, for a time-base of four thousand years, four times the thousand he has actually lived.
w05.095: Sadler's time-base arithmetic: compared with time actually lived, a human being has a time-base twice as long, an Adjuster-fused ascender one four times as long
w05.097: Sadler's theory runs as follows. A finite creature is bound to time just to the degree that it is wholly confined to the present moment. When we draw experience from the past, foresee the consequences of our acts in the future, and weave both together with wisdom into present decisions, we begin to step free of time. On this view a human being escapes time at twice the rate at which time flows, and a fused ascender at four times that rate.
w05.098: Pushed to the limit, the arithmetic goes like this. At a million years of age one would have a time-base of four million years. At a trillion years, roughly the age of the Andronover nebula, mother of our sun, the time-base would be four trillion years. By the time one enters the post-Ultimate age, having lived through the whole span that Sadler calculates for the master universe, one could comprehend four times that span. If our grasp of time grows four times faster than time itself, then, given ample time, even the quantity of eternity might become partly comprehensible, or at least far less daunting. That is Sadler's conclusion.
w05.101: The figures two and four are not revealed. Sadler himself hedges the whole calculation with an "if" about the merit of his reasoning. The point of the arithmetic is not precision but direction. Eternity is not a room one enters through a door on a given day; it is a country that becomes gradually familiar as more of the past and the future are woven into the present. This points the same way as the teaching that circular simultaneity will increasingly displace the consciousness of linear sequence [130:7.5].
w05.103: Experiential growth beyond the ultimate level means breaking through every earlier limit of growth. Sadler observes that this is the third such breakthrough, and that each time God established a new need in a new domain of experience by "subtracting" something from existing conditions.
w05.104: Three challenges God issued by taking something away (Sadler's scheme)
w05.106: The perfect beings of Paradise and Havona
Limit of original perfection → evolutionary growth added
w05.107: Possibility of finite experience, in outer space
Limit of finite growth → absonite growth
w05.108: Possibility of finite and absonite experience, in the Cosmos Infinite
Citizens of the completed master universe
Limit of relative growth → absolute growth
w05.109: Sadler expects the third challenge to be the prospect of the Cosmos Infinite. Its native beings would be incapable of either finite or absonite experience. The effort to make up for that lack is the Absolute Adventure itself, and in the course of it the citizens of the master universe would enter upon growth of an absolute kind.
w05.110: All three cases share one shape. God sets a challenge before those who dwell in a nuclear universe; they respond by serving and ministering in a new, outer, cytoplasmic domain; and in so doing they pass the old limit. Taking something away looks like creating a deficiency, but in Sadler's eyes the empty place is exactly where the next growth occurs.
w05.111: 5. The Capacity of the Finaliters (orig. pp. 106–107)
w05.112: What prospect awaits the finaliters in a post-Ultimate age, when finite and absonite growth alike are over? In the second age they came to know the Father finitely; through the four post-Supreme ages they experienced Him ultimately. With all relative growth finished, the only growth that could remain is absolute.
w05.113: Sadler judges the prospect bright. The evidence in the text is not abundant, he says, but it is enough to support this view, and it rests on two foundations. First, the finaliter possesses personality, a gift from God. Personality can express itself and grow on finite and absonite levels, and, though it cannot encompass the absolute level, it can penetrate it and grow within it. Second, the finaliter is fused with a fragment of God. As already noted, the Adjuster brings "⟦Q 112:7.1⟧a phase of qualified potential absoluteness⟦/Q⟧" [112:7.1]: a quality latent at the moment of fusion, not immediately evident, but certain to be realized in the far future.
w05.114: Sadler infers that this absoluteness is limited in the quantity of its outward self-expression but not in the quality of its inward self-realization. It is the same distinction The Urantia Book draws regarding the function of the Trinity Absolute.
w05.116: Since both gifts, personality and the Adjuster, come from God, it is not unreasonable to credit both with a potential for absolute growth. Sadler therefore concludes that finaliters can keep growing in the post-Ultimate age, that nothing can halt that growth, and that, quantitatively, they will never finish growing in it. Theirs is a destiny absolute in quality but not infinite in quantity: to seek God as the Absolute without ever knowing all of God as the Absolute. Always more, forever more, yet never all. The text describes the finaliters' next course this way:
w05.118: 6. The Cosmos Infinite: An Endless Cytoplasm (orig. p. 107)
w05.119: If Havona forms the core of the grand universe, and that larger domain in turn forms the core of the four outer space levels, of what is the master universe the nucleus? Sadler's answer is a possible Cosmos Infinite, an unending cytoplasm and the final antithesis. This cytoplasm would have to be unlike anything that has gone before, from the circuits of Havona to the Quartan Space Level. If the central universe is pre-creative and the master universe creative and evolving, Sadler suggests, the last universe of infinity may be "super-creative."
w05.121: Sadler conjectures that this endless universe will be experiential and yet post-finite and post-absonite, and perhaps existential and experiential at once. The idea is not foreign to the text, which describes the Deity Absolute in just such terms.
w05.123: Does the notion of an endless universe collide with the idea that space is limited at any given moment? Sadler answers that the two can be held together if space is assumed to expand faster than creation. That space reaches out past the presently known bounds of the master universe is certain. The Urantia Book says little about this far-future universe, but in Sadler's judgment its eventual appearance is clearly in view.
w05.125: Sadler's "Cosmos Infinite" comes from the Urantia Book term "cosmos-infinite" (106:6.3, 106:7.4). In the text, however, the word refers only hypothetically to an illimitable cosmos beyond the master universe. It is Sadler who shapes it into a definite final creation and capitalizes it as a proper name. This book keeps his capitalized form when speaking of his construct and the hyphenated form when quoting the text.
w05.126: 7. Adjusting to Infinity: The Parable of the Playing Field (orig. pp. 107–109)
w05.127: Sadler expects adjustment to infinity, like adjustment to eternity, to be gradual. No one will look out one day on star-filled space and suddenly realize, "So this is infinity." Instead, infinity becomes familiar little by little as one notices the milestones that mark the passage from the finite into the superfinite. Words such as absolute, eternal, and infinite carry no real meaning for us. Rather than drown in a flood of ponderous language, it is better to gain even a small feeling for the truth at some cost to fact. Sadler therefore offers a story as a "concept-symbol."
w05.128: In brief, the story runs like this. A college student, after long practice, becomes a starter on the football team and scores the winning touchdown in the big game. Afterward the coach leads him out onto the darkened field and switches on the lights. The goal line he crossed turns out to be merely the starting line of a ten-thousand-yard field that stretches farther than the eye can see.
w05.129: The coach tells him he may stay on the old field and help the younger players until he feels ready. For a time he enjoys being an assistant, but in the end curiosity outweighs contentment. He takes on the team of the great field, and after a far longer struggle he scores again. When the coach says there is something more to show him, the young man asks first: is this one a million yards? The story closes with the coach asking how he knew.
w05.130: The parable of the playing field: each goal line crossed opens a field a hundred times larger
w05.131: As the present commentator reads it, three meanings are folded into the story. The goal line is always the starting line of the next field, mirroring the structure of the post-Ultimate periods. The new field is never forced on anyone, and before moving on the hero helps those who come after him, just as the citizens of a nucleus serve the next generation before they go outward. And the second surprise is smaller than the first. Adjusting to infinity, the parable suggests, does not mean measuring all of it but growing at home among fields that keep opening without end.
w05.132: The post-Ultimate age is a Final Age that begins in time but has no end, the mirror image of the first age.
w05.133: An eternal age need not be monotonous: as with light and life and its seven stages, it unfolds in periods with attainable goals, the last of each series opening a new series.
w05.134: Sadler holds that a sense of the quantity of eternity grows gradually, and calculates that a human has a time-base twice the time lived and a fused ascender four times; this is analogical reasoning, not revelation.
w05.135: Three times God opened new needs and new growth by withholding something: original perfection, finite experience, and finite and absonite experience together.
w05.136: Thanks to two gifts, personality and the Adjuster, finaliters keep growing after the Ultimate, toward a destiny absolute in quality yet endless in quantity.
w05.137: The playing-field parable shows that adjusting to infinity is a slow growing-accustomed, with a new field opening beyond every goal line.
w05.139: The Last Story, Chapter XII, The Impossible Synthesis (pp. 110–115)
w05.140: Sadler sets out in nine steps why experiential Deities and Trinities appear at all. The reason, he says, is that a separation between Paradise and the Eternal Son, deliberately left unresolved by God, is worked out level by level through power-personality synthesis. The synthesis of the third level, however, would require exhausting infinity, so it can never be completed. Sadler names this the “Barrier of Infinity” and the “Impasse of the Absolutes,” and concludes that the Trinity of Trinities will never fill its second level.
w05.141: 1. The Ground of Experiential Deity and Trinity (orig. pp. 110–112)
w05.143: Sadler has followed master-universe history from time's dawn to the ages after the sixth. Its first great movement closed with the first synthesis, when God the Supreme emerged; its second closed with the second synthesis, the emergence of God the Ultimate. Now he asks: why do experiential Deities evolve and eventuate? Why are there two? Will there be a third?
w05.144: Beneath all of this lies the plan of God laid down in the eternal past. To read that plan, Sadler goes all the way back to the Zero Age and arranges what actually took place into nine steps.
w05.145: Why experiential Deity appears: Sadler's nine steps
w05.147: The three Absolutes are bound into one in the Universal Absolute
w05.148: The Eternal Son (thesis) and nonspiritual, impersonal Paradise (antithesis) stand apart
w05.149: The Paradise Trinity forms from the union of the three Persons
Not a synthesis but theses superimposed
w05.150: With Havona, finite and absonite levels are projected
w05.151: The Trinity reflected on each level becomes the potential of an experiential Deity
Seeds of God the Supreme, Ultimate, and Absolute
w05.152: On each level, power is gathered and unified with spirit personality through mind
The method for solving the problem left open
w05.153: The achievements of the Supreme Creators become one with the spirit person of Supremacy
w05.154: The first experiential Trinity unifies the whole master universe
w05.155: The three Absolutes, existentially one, must be synthesized experientially
The task of the second experiential Trinity
w05.157: The key to the nine steps is the second. When God brought forth the Eternal Son, the thesis of Deity, He brought forth Paradise, its antithesis, as well. The Son is the absolute personality; Paradise is the absolute of patterns, neither personal nor spiritual.
w05.159: According to Sadler, God did not synthesize these two absolute actualities. He co-ordinated them through mind and otherwise left them apart, a problem reserved for the experiential Deities and Trinities still to come. On the side of potentials, by contrast, synthesis was present from the start.
w05.161: Even the Paradise Trinity of the third step is, for Sadler, not a synthesis but one thesis laid upon another. Existential Deity is wholly unified, yet it remains separated from nondeity reality except for the co-ordination of mind.
w05.162: The Trinity reflected on every level
w05.163: When Havona appears, God projects the finite and absonite levels in addition to the absolute. In the first age all three levels were existential. The second age opens at the dawn of time with the appearance of experiential reality. Because the Paradise Trinity had always pervaded all three levels, Sadler reasons, its presence must have been reflected on each, and when experiential reality was created these reflections became the potentials of three experiential Deities: the spirit person of God the Supreme at the finite level, God the Ultimate at the absonite level, and, at the absolute level, God the Absolute latent within the Deity Absolute. The text, too, says that the three experiential Deities lay latent in the existential Trinity.
w05.165: For these potentials to become personalized as actual Deities, the problem God deliberately left unsolved must be solved. What is to be done with Paradise? Put differently, how is the whole of actual reality on the finite, absonite, and absolute levels to be gathered into one? Sadler sees only one method: power-personality synthesis. On each level the totality of power is assembled and, through the action of mind, unified with the spirit personality of Deity. One might describe it as mind mastering energy-matter and, by the choice of personality, bringing it under the leading of spirit.
w05.167: On the finite level the power of the Almighty Supreme becomes one with the spirit person of Supremacy, and the Supreme Being emerges. At the absonite level the first experiential Trinity unifies the whole master universe, and God the Ultimate completes His growth. What remains is the synthesis of the absolute level. This outline is, in effect, a summary of the entire study.
w05.168: 2. Infinity as a Barrier, the Absolutes at an Impasse (orig. pp. 112–113)
w05.170: The problem facing the second experiential Trinity can be put briefly. The three Absolutes of potentiality are infinite, but this Trinity is not, for the Supreme and the Ultimate are experiential Deities derived from the existential Paradise Trinity.
w05.171: The scope of power-personality synthesis has widened at every stage. Supremacy embraced the whole finite, the totality of finite meaning-value in the grand universe. Ultimacy synthesized the whole absonite, the totality of absonite meaning-value in the master universe. If God the Absolute could appear experientially, He would have to embrace the totality of experiential meaning-value in the Cosmos Infinite, a universe without end. And that totality is infinity. Here Sadler brings out the old paradox: what happens when an irresistible force meets an immovable fact? The irresistible force of the Trinity Absolute has come face to face with the immovable fact of eternal infinity.
w05.173: At each level the unification of experiential Deity left nothing out: it took in things together with their meanings and values, matter along with mind and spirit, and facts as well as ideas and relations. On the finite and absonite levels the process could run its full course because the grand universe and the master universe were bounded. Each had an "outside." The final level has no bounds. What could lie outside a creation that is infinite?
w05.174: Sadler examines what this last synthesis would demand under three aspects. Physically, the Cosmos Infinite would have to be materially completed. Spiritually, the infinite potential within the Deity Absolute would have to be fully actualized in experience. Personally, deified and undeified potentials alike would have to be unified within one Absolute who could comprehend and contact both. Such a task knows neither end nor limit, neither an outside nor a beyond. Infinity is not something that can be used up quantitatively. The text, too, pictures the level of God the Absolute as the place where Deity exhausts its potential for personalization.
w05.176: So Sadler reaches his conclusion. What an infinite Trinity accomplished existentially, a subinfinite Trinity cannot accomplish experientially. The Trinity Absolute can begin this work and pursue it without end, but it can never complete it. Therefore God the Absolute cannot emerge from the infinite potential of the Deity Absolute. This is what Sadler calls the “Barrier of Infinity,” the “Impasse of the Absolutes.”
w05.177: Sadler and the Text: The Outlook for God the Absolute
w05.178: The Urantia Book also doubts the full unification of the Trinity Absolute. Yet the text does not close the door there. Pointing out that trinitization can achieve what is otherwise unattainable, it leaves open the possibility that God the Absolute will one day become factual.
w05.180: The text also names God the Absolute "⟦Q 106:6.6⟧the third and last of the experiential Deities⟦/Q⟧" [106:6.6]. Sadler's "impossible" goes a step beyond the text's "doubt." His conclusion rests on the premise that infinity would have to be exhausted quantitatively; the text leaves open by what means the task might be accomplished.
w05.181: 3. The Trinity of Trinities, Never Completed (orig. pp. 114–115)
w05.183: Even if the Trinity Absolute cannot be unified, its mere factualization makes one great thing possible: the union of the three Trinities, the Trinity of Trinities. Its members are not three Deities but three Trinities, a Deity association of three levels. On the first level the three Trinities are joined; on the second the three experiential Deities seek union; on the third there must be some final Deity reality.
w05.185: The character of the three Trinities (Sadler's scheme)
w05.190: Sadler says this is the goal toward which the long, long growth of the master universe has been aiming: the composite Trinity of all Deity, existential and experiential together, a "thesis of theses," the final Deity thesis.
w05.192: This threefold Trinity, however, has three vertical levels. On the first level all three Trinities exist in fact. Of the three experiential Deities who belong on the second level, two are already factual: God the Supreme and God the Ultimate. The missing one is God the Absolute: the Deity Absolute has not been personalized, not even in a limited form.
w05.194: The three levels of the Trinity of Trinities; on the second level the third seat, that of God the Absolute, stands empty
w05.195: The experiential personalization of God the Absolute depends on the unification of the Trinity Absolute, and that unification depends on exhausting the whole of infinity. Yet infinity cannot be exhausted quantitatively. The Trinity of Trinities can therefore be formed, because all three of its member Trinities are factual, but its second level cannot be filled. And if the second level cannot be filled, there is no way even to guess what the third level might be. The study halts once more before the “Barrier of Infinity.”
w05.196: Infinity approached from within, infinity approached from without
w05.197: Here, it seems, the master universe's story reaches its close. That immense experiential creation gives rise to two experiential Deities and two experiential Trinities and prepares the ground on which the Trinity of Trinities becomes factual. There it reaches an impasse. The Trinity Absolute cannot be unified; God the Absolute therefore cannot be power-personalized; and the second level of the threefold Trinity cannot be completed.
w05.198: God is not frustrated by this. In Sadler's words, God dwells in eternity and so approaches infinity existentially, "from within." Experiential Deity, by contrast, must approach infinity "from without," and to penetrate the whole of infinity experientially from without would require another eternity. The argument has come full circle. To exhaust infinity one would have to reach the end of eternity, yet eternity is infinite and infinity is eternal. Not even the Paradise Trinity can experientialize the Deity Absolute, for that is possible only to an experiential Trinity. Sadler closes the chapter by observing that no one can do what even the Trinity of infinity cannot do.
w05.199: Sadler's conclusion sounds like a dead end, but read together with the playing-field parable of the previous chapter it takes on a different meaning. Having no end is not a failure; it is also a promise that growth will never stop. The text confesses that it does not know what would happen if the second level of the Trinity of Trinities were unified, yet it states the direction plainly.
w05.201: Sadler arranges everything from the Zero Age to the emergence of God the Ultimate into nine steps to explain why experiential Deities and Trinities appear.
w05.202: In Sadler's interpretation, God synthesized the potentials (the three Absolutes) existentially but left the actuals (the Eternal Son and Paradise) unsynthesized, a problem for the experiential Deities to solve.
w05.203: Synthesis on the third level would require exhausting infinity, so the subinfinite Trinity Absolute can begin and continue the work but never finish it; Sadler calls this the “Barrier of Infinity” and the “Impasse of the Absolutes.”
w05.204: The Urantia Book doubts the full unification of the Trinity Absolute yet keeps open the possibility that God the Absolute will appear through trinitization; Sadler's "impossible" goes a step beyond the text.
w05.205: The Trinity of Trinities can be formed, but with the seat of God the Absolute empty on its second level, it cannot be completed.
w05.206: God approaches infinity from within, while experiential Deity must approach it from without, so the experiential conquest of infinity has no end; this can also be read as a promise of endless growth.
